angle: broadcast graphics and scoreboards — lower thirds, chevrons, bold numerals, motion-implying stripes, high contrast at 42px, built around the DiscBattle score moment

families.name: Chevron Run
families.concept: A broadcast transition wipe frozen on the disc: a run of fat chevrons over a wash band, the leading one carrying a bright inner nose.

seed.tilt: -17..17 deg rotation of the whole run
seed.phase: -34..34 units of travel along the run axis
seed.arm: 96..140 units of chevron half-height (how open the V is)
seed.chip_deg: -46..46, scaled to slide the cue chip along the top edge of the band

params.base: disc body fill; its luminance sets the cue chip ink, and the accent's sets the lit nose ink, so both stay legible on any palette
params.accent: chevron mass, wash band, speed rules, rim ring, cue-chip outline, label plate
params.label: aria-label and <title> at every target; the first 10 characters are set in the name plate at 220 only

targets.42: 3 chevrons, no speed rules, fattest strokes
targets.96: 4 chevrons plus the two speed rules

families.name: Score Bug
families.concept: The lower-third score bug laid across the disc: a hard accent band with a logo chip, a run of tally segments (some lit) and a clock colon.

seed.y_off: -26..36 units of band height on the face
seed.lit: 1..4 of the segments read as lit
seed.chip_right: which end of the band carries the logo chip
seed.tick_shift: -18..18 units sliding the cue ticks above the band

params.base: disc body fill; its luminance picks the colour of the hairline rule above the band
params.accent: the band itself, the chevron inside the chip, the cue ticks, the rim, the unlit segments (as a darkened mix) and the label plate
params.label: aria-label and <title> at every target; first 10 characters in the plate at 220

families.name: Sweep Clock
families.concept: The shot clock: a tick ring with heavier quarter ticks, a filled sweep wedge and one bright hand at the leading edge.

seed.start: -118..-62 deg where the wedge opens (near twelve o'clock)
seed.ring_shift: 0..14 deg rotation of the tick ring
seed.pip_r: 96..138 units -- how far out the lit pip sits inside the wedge

params.base: disc body fill and hub fill; its luminance picks the hand, quarter-tick and pip colour
params.accent: wedge fill and outline, minor ticks, ring, hub ring, rim, label plate
params.label: aria-label and <title> at every target; first 10 characters in the plate at 220

single.details: False drops the eyebrow, note and flight cells; the art grows and the name carries the card

design.standard: 660x300 two-up with a centre scoreboard block
design.stacked: 440x424 two lower thirds with a per-row score plate

battle.score: scores read from card['scores'] (dict by presentationId, dict by index, or list), then participant['score']; missing values render an en dash. The leading half of the scoreboard fills with that disc's colour and the trailing numeral dims. card['winner'] / ['manualWinner'] overrides the leader and tags the header; card['highlight'] rings a participant.
battle.details: False drops the eyebrows and flight cells; art, name and score remain

notes: Two colours in, four colours used: every family derives `edge` (contrasts with the base, carries the one bright live mark) and `knock` (contrasts with the accent, used only on top of an accent mass) by luminance, so nothing goes mushy on the pale warm palette or the dark one. Identity is five RNG draws taken before any target branching, so 42/96/220 are the same disc at three levels of detail rather than three different discs. Cards inline the art under a placed <g> with per-participant id namespacing instead of a nested <svg>: a host stylesheet that sizes `svg { width: … }` — the tournament's own rasterizer does exactly this — cannot resize the disc out of its slot. Previews and the self-check are reproducible: `python3 build_preview.py` then `python3 selfcheck.py` (300 checks, corpus digest printed).
